quirks: Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties; pre-1811 records are filed under the parent counties.

Church items seek Thomas's death entry listing Patrick as surviving family. Tax items track succession from Thomas to Patrick on the same property. Cemetery items look for shared family plots. Military items seek pension files naming Patrick's father or Patrick's own service records naming Thomas. No item pursues a relative's own record for its own sake; all serve to establish or corroborate the parent-child relationship with Patrick as the subject.

dimensions.name: Sequencing logic
dimensions.rationale: Sequence numbers reflect defensible search order: pli_007 (FamilySearch probate, free/indexed) before pli_008 (Ancestry probate, paid/indexed fallback). pli_009 (church, fully indexed) follows. pli_010 (tax) and pli_011 (cemetery) are secondary sources. pli_012 (military/FAN) is last, as required for parentage questions. Fallback chain is explicit: pli_008 has fallback_for='pli_007'. Rationales explain placement: FamilySearch probate is 'primary search,' Ancestry is 'fallback if FamilySearch image-browse yields nothing.' The 1860-1870 anchor is consistent across all items.

dimensions.name: Jurisdiction accuracy
dimensions.rationale: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania is correctly identified for the 1860-1870 period. The place_search tool confirmed 'Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, United States' as a County with dateRange '+1811/', meaning it existed continuously from 1811 onward — well before and through 1860-1870. No boundary changes or pre-statehood jurisdictional issues apply to this period in Pennsylvania. All six plan items correctly name 'Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania' as the jurisdiction.

dimensions.name: Plan mode and lifecycle
dimensions.rationale: The skill correctly chose supersede mode: pl_002 was active with pli_006 still 'in_progress' (probate 1870-1890), and new information (Thomas's death ~1865) invalidated that date range. The lifecycle was handled correctly: pl_002.status was set to 'superseded' (not deleted or edited in place), pl_003 was created as 'active', and exactly one active plan now exists for q_001. Prior plan items remain intact as audit trail. The new plan's narrative explicitly references the superseded plan and explains why the prior date range was wrong. No duplicate active plans; no in-place edits to completed/superseded items.
